Versões desconhecidas ou chunkSizeLog2 fora do limite passam por varredura estrutural por chunk: cada candidato é validado e os chunks válidos são importados com partial:true. Chunks com log2 acima do limite são subdivididos em 16³ sem perda de resolução. Orçamento estourado importa subconjunto priorizado por densidade/proximidade à origem (nunca vazio). Relatório único no Output. Exporta SMOOTH_GRID_TOLERANT_VERSION. Spec: smoothGridTolerant153.spec.mjs (60 PASS); specs 131/132 continuam verdes.

entries.title: Interop sem perdas: preservação opaca de propriedades e classes desconhecidas
entries.description: A limitação 'tipos de propriedade sem suporte no import binário são ignorados com warning; classes desconhecidas no XML viram Folder' morreu por PRESERVAÇÃO OPACA (contrato interop-unknown-1, Parte 155): nada de adivinhar semântica de formato — o que era descartado agora é guardado byte a byte e reemitido na exportação. No import binário (.rbxl/.rbxm), propriedade com type id fora do formato vira carga opaca na instância (nome + type id + bytes crus, invisível no painel Properties) e o aviso agregado nomeia classe+propriedade+id dizendo 'preservada', não 'ignorada'; no export a coluna PROP original volta byte-idêntica (round-trip provado na spec). No XML (.rbxlx/.rbxmx), classe desconhecida continua virando Folder no editor (a árvore funciona), mas guarda o ClassName original e o bag completo de propriedades, e o writer reemite a classe e as propriedades originais na exportação — filhos preservados nos dois mundos. Limites anti-exploit dedicados (RBX_UNKNOWN_LIMITS: 256 KB por blob, 16 registros e 1 MB por instância, 512 registros por arquivo, bag com até 128 propriedades) e entrada malformada nunca lança exceção. Núcleo puro e testável em Node: src/interop/rbxUnknown.js; guardião novo tools/tests/rbxUnknown155.spec.mjs (43 asserções). Resíduos honestos que continuam descartados: chunks binários desconhecidos, Refs de classes desconhecidas e cargas opacas em serviços do place.

entries.title: BasePart completo: Reflectance, GetMass, Resize, juntas e network ownership
entries.description: Sete membros clássicos de BasePart saíram do backlog do fix 122.2 e viraram implementação real (contrato basepart-members-1, Parte 143): part.Reflectance lê/escreve pelo Lua com clamp 0..1 na escrita (espelhado no datamodel e consumido pelo render de iluminação); part:GetMass() devolve massa de verdade (volume pela forma — Block/Truss, Ball π/6, Cylinder π/4 no eixo X, Wedge 1/2, CornerWedge 1/6, MeshPart/Union por bounding box — × densidade da tabela OFICIAL de materiais do Roblox); part:Resize(normalId, delta) cresce SÓ no eixo da face, desloca a posição em delta/2 na direção da face e devolve false sem alterar nada se violar o tamanho mínimo de 0.05 (nunca NaN); part:BreakJoints() remove toda junta (Weld/WeldConstraint/Motor6D/Snap/Rotate/Glue) conectada à part; part:MakeJoints() cria Welds apenas entre partes encostadas cujas superfícies em contato são juntáveis (Weld/Glue/Studs/Inlet/Universal — Smooth NÃO junta) e nunca duplica junta entre o mesmo par; e part:SetNetworkOwner(player|nil)/part:GetNetworkOwner() controlam o dono da simulação de rede com semântica Roblox — nil = servidor, só o Server pode definir (erro pt-BR no Client, anti-exploit), erro em part Anchored, e o estado vive num Map por instância dentro de src/runtime/ (nunca no datamodel). O núcleo é puro e testável headless (partMass.js + partJoints.js, fatias A/B do agente-part-core); o bridge só injeta acessores (getDescendants/getProperty/createInstance/destroy/touchingParts — mesma detecção AABB do GetTouchingParts). IntelliSense documenta os 7 em BasePart, a Validação Mestre ganhou o check integration.partApi143 e o bullet BasePart saiu do backlog do README (contagem atualizada). Guardiões: tools/tests/partApi143.spec.mjs + apiSurface122.spec.mjs. Fora do escopo (não implementados): SetNetworkOwnershipAuto/GetNetworkOwnershipAuto.

entries.title: Camera:Interpolate gira de verdade: a pose da câmera preserva rotação
entries.description: Fecho da cadeia do contrato camera-interp-1 (Parte 144): a escrita da pose da câmera deixou de descartar a rotação. writeCameraProps agora grava o CFrame COM o quaternion da pose (makeCFrame de 7 argumentos, a mesma fábrica da Parte 111) e a guarda anti-spam (lastSyncKey) passou a incluir a rotação — antes ela era montada só com posições arredondadas, então uma mudança apenas de rotação com a posição parada era engolida pela guarda e NUNCA sincronizava: era o bug que impedia o slerp do Camera:Interpolate (núcleo puro cameraInterp.js + case do bridge, fatias A/B da Parte 144) de aparecer na tela. updateScriptedPose segue honrando a Parte 111 (quat não-identidade manda na mira; sem quat vale o Focus clássico) e agora carrega o quaternion adiante na pose; getLastRenderPose devolve a rotação (GetRenderCFrame do bridge depende disso), inclusive com shake ativo — o shake é posicional e a rotação da pose base passa adiante. Custo zero: pose sem rotação gera exatamente a mesma chave e os mesmos números de hoje (quat identidade, escrita legada), e os modos look-at (Attach/Watch/Track e zoomToExtents) resetam a rotação para identidade. A Validação Mestre ganhou o check integration.camRender144 e a limitação correspondente saiu do README. Guardião: tools/tests/camRender144.spec.mjs.

entries.title: Tool.Grip agora é um CFrame de verdade (posição + orientação)
entries.description: A pega da Tool deixou de ser só posicional: ler tool.Grip devolve um CFrame completo montado dos 4 vetores reais do schema (GripPos/GripForward/GripRight/GripUp) via gripToCFrame (contrato tool-grip-1, módulo puro src/runtime/gripMath.js), e atribuir tool.Grip = CFrame decompõe a rotação com cframeToGrip e grava os 4 vetores — orientações de pega personalizadas (espada de lado, tocha inclinada) finalmente sobrevivem à leitura e à escrita pelo script. Atribuir não-CFrame continua lançando o mesmo LuaError de antes (Grip deve receber um valor CFrame), CFrames só-posição seguem gravando GripPos idêntico ao comportamento antigo (vetores ficam nos defaults) e, com os 4 defaults, o Grip lido é a IDENTIDADE — custo zero e compatibilidade total com projetos existentes. Vetores degenerados no datamodel (zero, colineares, NaN) caem nos defaults sem nunca produzir NaN. IntelliSense ganhou as entradas de Tool (Grip, GripPos, GripForward, GripRight, GripUp). Parte 140 protegida por tools/tests/gripBridge140.spec.mjs.

entries.title: Bones: rotação real em Transform/WorldCFrame (CFrame completo)
entries.description: A componente de rotação dos CFrames de Bone deixou de ser ignorada ao posar bones em runtime (pendência pós-Parte 111 encerrada): bone.Transform aceita e devolve CFrame COMPLETO — posição + rotação real (ordem YXZ, a mesma do skinning do Fix 91.12) —, com a rotação persistida em TransformRotation (Vector3 em graus; rotação identidade zera TransformRotation, fidelidade Roblox). Bone.WorldCFrame e Bone.WorldPosition agora são a COMPOSIÇÃO da hierarquia de Bones (posição E rotação via mulBoneCF, não soma de posições; no host Anchored compõe também a rotação da part), e GetRelativeTransform/GetRelativeTransformAll devolvem CFrames compostos com rotação. Custo zero sem rotação: com quat identidade o caminho e os números são idênticos aos de antes. IntelliSense documenta a classe Bone (Transform, TransformRotation, WorldCFrame, WorldPosition, GetRelativeTransform/All), a Validação Mestre ganha o check scenario.boneCFrameRotation (avisa escrita de rotação em bone.Transform sem Bones na cena e conflito Transform × TransformRotation) e a limitação saiu do README. Guardião: tools/tests/boneApi139.spec.mjs.

entries.title: Legacy Engine Parity: Stream-In Identity & Full Debugger
entries.description: The legacy JS interpreter closes the last documented streaming divergence: with StreamingEnabled, clients running the legacy engine now hand scripts a brand-new Lua identity when an instance streams back into range, exactly like the official Luau VM (Part 81) - references captured before the stream-out become stale husks, oldRef == newRef is false after a stream-out/in cycle, stale references sent through remotes arrive as nil, and the identity layer is zero-cost by design (servers and sessions without StreamingEnabled keep the exact same objects as before). The legacy engine also reaches full Debugger parity with the WASM VM (Part 77): breakpoints, step into/over/out - including stepping into coroutines created with coroutine.create/wrap/task.spawn and returning to the resumer - call stack, locals, logpoints, and a Watch with write-back (typing hp = 50 while paused writes the real local/upvalue/global of the paused frame). Studio Settings now reports the legacy engine as full parity (streaming identity + debugger) instead of a fallback without native debugging, Master Validation gains a check that fails if a stream-out/in cycle ever reuses the old identity on the legacy engine, and the corresponding limitation was removed from the README (Part 136, guarded by tools/tests/legacyDebugUi136.spec.mjs).

entries.title: Navmesh dinâmico: obstáculos em movimento replanejam caminhos
entries.description: A limitação de navmesh só de geometria estática acabou: partes que se movem durante o Play agora entram no navmesh como obstáculos dinâmicos rastreados por um índice espacial, disparando Blocked/Unblocked reais nos waypoints e replanejamento automático do caminho (auto-repath) com cooldown mínimo por path e teto global anti-exploit. CreatePath ganhou 4 agentParameters novos — AgentDynamicAvoidance, AgentAutoRepath, AgentRepathCooldown e AgentPredictSeconds — e Path ganhou o evento Recomputed(reason, waypointCount) e as propriedades readOnly IsDynamic e RepathCount (extensões do projeto). O click-to-move replaneja sozinho quando um obstáculo cruza a rota. No editor, o novo toggle View > Show Dynamic Obstacles desenha as caixas amarelas dos obstáculos (mais intensas quando em movimento), os waypoints bloqueados em vermelho e um pulso curto no ponto de partida quando o caminho é replanejado — custo ~zero desligado e zero regressão enquanto o snapshot não expõe os dados dinâmicos. Parte 135 protegida por 3 specs guardiões (núcleo, watcher/repath e UI/docs — navmeshUi135).

entries.title: Sons da CDN com 3D, efeitos e reverb (degrau tag-graph)
entries.description: Novo degrau na escada de degradação do áudio da CDN, entre bytes e tag: quando a CDN libera CORS de mídia (sonda determinística com timeout, cache negativo com TTL e dedupe — audioTagGraph.js), o elemento <audio> (com crossOrigin anonymous) é roteado para DENTRO do grafo Web Audio (MediaElementAudioSourceNode) e o som da CDN ganha a experiência completa SEM precisar baixar os bytes: espacialização 3D, SoundGroup, toda a cadeia de efeitos (Equalizer/Reverb/Distortion/Chorus/Compressor/Echo/Flange/PitchShift/Tremolo), reverb ambiente, doppler, VolumeScale pelo master e Volume até 10 — no playback, no preview e no PlayOnRemove. Erro de mídia no início degrada na hora para o degrau tag simples; falha de ambiente desliga o degrau com limpeza. ROBLOX_AUDIO_CDN_DIAG() agora mostra o degrau ativo por id nos quatro degraus (bytes | tag-graph | tag | jingle), o motivo de recusa do tag-graph por id (graphReasons) e a telemetria dos três núcleos. Ressalva dos degraus de tag: playbackRate clampado a [0.25, 4] pelo elemento de mídia.

entries.title: Sons importados tocam o arquivo real
entries.description: SoundId que aponta para um asset de áudio importado no Asset Manager (mp3/ogg/wav) agora é decodificado de verdade (decodeAudioData + fallback de parser WAV puro em audioDecode.js) no playback, no preview e no PlayOnRemove, com IsLoaded/TimeLength/evento Loaded corretos e cancelamento seguro de decodes pendentes (Stop/Pause/troca de SoundId/cliques rápidos). Arquivo corrompido não cai em síntese: IsLoaded fica false e o erro aparece no Output. Ids sem asset importado seguem com o jingle sintetizado determinístico. Spec headless audioDecode121 (40 checks).

entries.title: Physics: PrismaticConstraint Pulls Misaligned Attachments Into Alignment
entries.description: PrismaticConstraint no longer freezes the relative orientation captured at creation: the angular lock target is now the coincidence of the two attachment frames (slide axis + secondary axis), so misaligned attachments are PULLED until their axes line up, exactly like Roblox - previously the slider preserved the initial misalignment forever. The alignment reuses the joint's existing hard machinery (3-DOF angular PGS rows plus the NGS positional pass with the standard per-iteration clamps), so it holds under extreme load (a 50-mass carriage under 20x gravity stays aligned within 2 degrees while hard limits stop it), works with different axes on each attachment (the body rotates the full 90 degrees when Attachment1 slides along its local Y), corrects twist around the slide axis as well (full frame, not just the axis), adds no axial friction (the carriage still slides freely and motors/servos behave identically), and sleeps cleanly once aligned with no wake/sleep loop. The game layer now passes the attachment frames (axisB/refA/refB, same convention as the hinge from Part 119); at engine level, constructing a slider without axisB keeps the old snapshot behavior so existing integrations and tests are untouched. Degenerate inputs are sanitized (NaN/Infinity/zero axes fall back to canonical directions, references parallel to the axis get a fallback tangent). Pinned by a new 38-check contract suite (prismaticAlign120: 30-degree pull-in, twist correction, legacy snapshot preserved, free axial slide during alignment, extreme load with limits, motor in aligned mode, different attachment axes, insane-input fuzz, sleep, and the deep-review contracts - a 350-degree misalignment takes the 10-degree short path of the quaternion double cover instead of spinning the long way, an exact 180-degree flip converges without a saddle, and the alignment target is deterministic across rebuilds instead of re-freezing whatever sag the pair had at rebuild time) plus a self-checking in-game QA script (tools/qa/parte120-teste-prismatic-align.luau) with four scenes including a no-phantom-rotation control.

entries.title: Physics: Parts Now Rest Exactly on the Smooth Terrain Surface
entries.description: Fixed the global bug where parts and 3D models floated up to half a voxel (~2 studs) above smooth terrain while the character walked on it perfectly. Root cause: the project had TWO different definitions of the terrain surface - the character controller and the renderer used the smooth density field iso-surface 0.5 (tent blur, Part 92), while rigid bodies collided against BINARY voxel boxes whose flat top sits above the rendered relief on full ground. Cut at the root: the voxel-box collider was removed entirely and rigid bodies now collide against the exact same smooth field, through a new implicit-surface (SDF) shape in the physics engine. The shape queries signed distance and outward normal from the shared terrain sampler ((iso - density)/|gradient|, clamped so deep points can never catapult), supports box/convex and sphere narrowphase with multi-point manifolds (a box on flat ground rests on a stable 4-point manifold and sleeps), treats water as non-solid (buoyancy from Part 112 keeps handling flotation), and hardens against hostile fields (null/NaN/throwing samplers are neutralized per sample). Terrain raycasts were unified onto the same surface: the voxel DDA still finds the hit cell, then the hit is refined to the smooth iso-crossing by bisection with the field normal, so picking, tools and in-game workspace:Raycast agree with both the visual relief and physics rest height (water hits stay on the binary voxel, matching its dedicated wave runtime). The terrain body builder is now a pure injected-data module, testable headless. The deep review of Part 119 also fixed a wrap-around bug in the new hinge limits at exactly +/-180 degrees: a pair resting on such a limit read a phantom ~2*pi violation, so it could never sleep and the positional pass spun it forever; limit error is now measured on the circle (shortest signed path, no sign clamps - Lower == Upper keeps correcting sagging below the lock angle). New 24-check suite (terrainSdf1191: analytic-plane settling, parity of box/sphere rest height with the character's groundAt, slope support, water pass-through, tunneling guard, hostile-field and NaN-body fuzz, edit-rebuild) plus 6 new hinge checks (40 total), and a self-checking runtime QA script (tools/qa/fix1191-teste-colisao-terreno.luau).

entries.title: Physics: HingeConstraint Hard Limits in the Solver
entries.description: HingeConstraint no longer enforces LowerAngle/UpperAngle as a proportional servo in the game layer (which extreme loads could temporarily overpower): the limits are now hard solver rows, closing the last soft joint limit left after Parts 108-110 (Rope/Prismatic/BallSocket). The hinge angle is measured inside the engine by swing-twist decomposition of the attachment frames (robust even when the axis is momentarily bent under load, where projecting reference vectors degenerates), using the exact same sign convention as the game layer and the motor (Part 108 fix). Each end of the interval is a unilateral angular PGS row with warm starting - completely free inside the limits, resisting only outward motion at the ends - plus an NGS positional pass that rotates the pair back inside the interval directly on orientations with the standard per-iteration clamps. The limit wins against the motor by construction (solved after it in every iteration), continuous external torque cannot leak past the limit after first contact, and the degenerate LowerAngle == UpperAngle interval becomes a bilateral lock at that exact angle. The anti-freeze contract from Parts 108-110 extends to hinge limits: a sleeping body whose limit is violated (for example limits tightened at runtime) is woken so the error can never freeze. Runtime property edits sync every step like Rope/Prismatic/BallSocket, setters sanitize NaN/Infinity (previous value kept) and clamp to +/-180 degrees with upper >= lower, and a cheap always-on counter (limitActiveSteps) exposes limit activity. A new headless suite (hingeLimit119, 34 checks) pins the contracts: a 50-mass arm under 20x gravity stays within 1.5 degrees of the limit, free motion inside and with limits disabled, no energy gain resting on the limit, runtime tightening pulls the load back, motor pressed against both ends, continuous external torque, wake-on-violation with aggressive sleep, angle-sign parity with the game layer and fuzz inputs. A runtime QA script (tools/qa/parte119-teste-hinge-limites.luau) builds four self-checking scenes in-game.

entries.title: Physics: Real Buoyancy in Terrain Water
entries.description: Terrain water is no longer just a visual material: it is now a physical volume with real buoyancy. Every dynamic assembly that intersects water voxels receives Archimedes' force (water density 1, like Roblox) computed per Part from its real shape volume, so wood (0.35) and plastic (0.7) float at the correct depth (a wood cube rides ~35% submerged, plastic ~70%) while metal (7.85) sinks and rests on the bottom. The submerged fraction is sampled on an oriented grid of up to 27 points per Part with a smooth vertical kernel around the voxel surface, so forces ramp continuously instead of jumping in 4-stud voxel steps, and the upward force is applied at the centroid of the submerged volume - off-center buoyancy produces the natural righting torque, so planks and boats level themselves out. Linear drag proportional to the displaced water mass (applied at the same centroid) and exponential angular drag damp the bobbing; both are clamped so they can never reverse a velocity within a substep, making the response unconditionally stable even with extreme custom densities. Anti-exploit caps limit buoyancy to 20x the body weight (density 0.01 no longer rockets objects into orbit) and NaN/Infinity inputs are neutralized. The anti-freeze contract from Parts 108-110 extends to fluids: a sleeping body whose buoyancy exceeds its weight by more than a 15% hysteresis is woken (flooding an area lifts sleeping crates), while a body floating in equilibrium stays asleep with no wake/sleep loop. Fixing that properly also closed a pre-existing hidden bug: rebuilding terrain collision now wakes all dynamic bodies, so carving the ground from under a sleeping box no longer leaves it frozen in mid-air. To make water reachable from gameplay (and testable), Terrain:FillBlock, FillBall and Clear are now implemented in the Luau bridge (axis-aligned voxel fill with span caps; Enum.Material.Air erases; FillRegion raises a clear error since the VM has no Region3), emitting the same change event the editor tools use so visuals, collision and the water field rebuild together. Cheap always-on diagnostics (bodies in water, samples) are exposed through the physics stats. The buoyancy core is a pure Node-testable module pinned by a 37-check contract suite (waterBuoyancy112: exact Archimedes force, equilibrium depths per density, smooth monotonic surface kernel, righting torque sign, no phantom energy, sleep hysteresis, flood wake, quick rejection away from water, and fuzz with NaN/Infinity/zero gravity/degenerate sizes), plus a self-checking runtime QA script (tools/qa/parte112-teste-runtime.luau) with four in-game scenes.

entries.title: Scripting: CFrame With Real Rotation in the Luau VM
entries.description: The CFrame datatype in the Luau VM is no longer position-only: it now carries a real rotation (quaternion) using the exact same rotation convention as the physics engine and the viewport, so part.CFrame and part.Rotation always describe the same orientation. Previously CFrame.Angles and fromEulerAnglesXYZ were identity stubs, there was no CFrame * CFrame operator and no basis vectors, so canonical Roblox code like part.CFrame = part.CFrame * CFrame.Angles(0, dt, 0) - including the examples shipped in the built-in Help - crashed with an arithmetic error on userdata. The full documented API now works: constructors (new with position, position + lookAt target, or quaternion components; Angles; fromEulerAnglesXYZ/YXZ; fromOrientation; fromAxisAngle; lookAt; fromMatrix; identity), operators (CFrame * CFrame composition, CFrame * Vector3 rotating the vector, CFrame +/- Vector3), properties (Position, Rotation, RightVector/UpVector/LookVector plus X/Y/ZVector) and methods (Inverse, ToWorldSpace/ToObjectSpace, PointToWorldSpace/PointToObjectSpace, VectorToWorldSpace/VectorToObjectSpace, Lerp with spherical interpolation, ToEulerAnglesXYZ, ToOrientation, GetComponents). Reading part.CFrame builds the frame from Position + Rotation, and assigning part.CFrame writes both, so rotations survive the datamodel round trip. tostring(cframe) now prints the 12 components like Roblox. All the math lives in a pure, Node-testable module with anti-exploit sanitization (NaN/Infinity/degenerate axes fall back to identity instead of corrupting state), and the convention itself is pinned by contract tests (cframeVM111, 40 checks) so the VM, the physics and the renderer can never drift apart. A deep review then fixed six hidden gaps before they reached users: the 12-component CFrame.new(x, y, z, R00..R22) matrix constructor (previously misread as a quaternion call, producing garbage rotations), rotation silently dropped by CFrameValue and CFrame attributes (stored values came back position-only), value equality ignoring rotation (a rotation-only write was treated as a no-op and discarded), GetRenderCFrame returning a rotation-less frame, the missing ToAxisAngle method, and the Scriptable camera ignoring the rotation of an assigned CFrame (cam.CFrame = CFrame.new(eye, target) now really aims the view). A runtime QA script (tools/qa/parte111-cframe-runtime.luau) validates six self-checking scenes in-game, including the exact line that used to crash and a full GetComponents/ToAxisAngle roundtrip.

entries.title: Physics: BallSocket Hard Cone and Twist Limits (3/3)
entries.description: Third and final part attacking the joint-stretching limitation. BallSocketConstraint no longer enforces its cone limit as a soft angular-velocity correction in the game layer (which extreme loads could visibly overpower): the joint is now a first-class solver constraint. The cone limit is a unilateral angular PGS row with warm starting (it only resists opening, is completely free inside the cone) plus an NGS positional pass that rotates the pair back inside the cone directly on orientations with the standard per-iteration clamps, and it honors the anti-freeze contract: a sleeping body whose cone or twist is violated is woken so the error can never freeze. TwistLimitsEnabled/TwistLowerAngle/TwistUpperAngle, previously silently ignored, now work as native hard limits around the cone axis using the same machinery. Degenerate folds (joint bent to 180 degrees, where the constraint axis vanishes) recover through a fallback tangent axis, runtime property edits are synced every step like Rope/Prismatic, and all limit setters sanitize NaN/Infinity/negative inputs. A new headless suite (ballSocketCone110, 34 checks) pins the contracts: a 50-mass arm under 20x gravity stays within 1.5 degrees of the cone, free motion inside the cone and with limits disabled, no energy gain resting against the cone, runtime tightening pulls the load back, 180-degree fold recovery, twist held under continuous torque in both directions, wake-on-violation with aggressive sleep, fuzz inputs and a zero-angle cone. With this, contacts and every joint type are native solver constraints with real positional stabilization (Parts 108-110).

entries.title: Physics: Rope and Prismatic Are Now Native Solver Constraints (2/3)
entries.description: Second of three parts attacking the joint-stretching limitation. RopeConstraint and PrismaticConstraint no longer run as simplified per-step impulse corrections in the game layer: both are now first-class constraints inside the physics solver, solved together with contacts and the other joints (PGS velocity rows with warm starting plus NGS positional correction). The rope is a true unilateral distance constraint: it only resists stretching, never pushes, wakes sleeping bodies when taut (anti-freeze contract) and supports live Length edits (winches). The slider locks all three relative rotation axes and both perpendicular translations at solver level, with hard limits and Motor/Servo actuators solved as native rows, so heavy loads no longer bend or twist the carriage. Debugging the rope chain exposed a real solver flaw: chains of unilateral constraints with high mass ratios became a perpetual pogo (warm-started tension from the braking step was re-applied whole, launched the chain upward, the ropes went slack and the cycle repeated forever without settling; removing warm starting entirely was proven catastrophically worse, with unbounded stretching). Fixed by scaling velocity iterations with the number of active joints (+6 sweeps per joint, capped at 60, zero extra cost when no joints exist): a 9-rope chain with a 50x heavier tip under Roblox gravity and aggressive sleep tuning now settles tight (max stretch 1.2%) and falls asleep within 2 seconds. A new headless suite (jointNative109, 35 checks) pins the contracts: heavy loads, slack freedom in every direction, pendulum energy conservation, aggressive-sleep chains, runtime Length edits, perpendicular drift, motor speed, hard limits, closed-loop servo replicating the game layer, vertical crane under load, insane inputs and wake-on-stretch. A runtime QA script (tools/qa/parte109-teste-runtime.luau) builds four self-checking scenes automatically. A deep review then closed an anti-freeze gap: a sleeping slider pair whose hard limits were violated (for example limits tightened at runtime), or with perpendicular drift or unlocked relative orientation, is now woken like Rope and BallSocket already were (previously the error could freeze forever), and a degenerate slider axis (zero/NaN/Infinity) now falls back to a canonical axis instead of corrupting the joint (jointNative109 grew to 41 checks). Part 3/3 will give BallSocket a hard cone limit.

entries.title: Physics: Joints No Longer Freeze Stretched When Bodies Fall Asleep
entries.description: Runtime QA caught a real bug the headless tests missed: the in-game chain settled visibly stretched (total length 10.12 vs 9.50 nominal, one link gap frozen at 0.49) while the equivalent headless scene stayed tight. Root cause: the game layer uses aggressive sleep tuning (sleepSpeedLimit 0.4, sleepTimeLimit 0.8) and computes masses from size and density, so tiny chain links (mass 0.112) carrying a 50x heavier tip slowed below the sleep threshold while the joint error from the initial drop was still large - and sleeping bodies are invisible to the NGS position pass, freezing the stretch forever. Two fixes: (1) anti-freeze contract in the joint position solver - if a joint's positional error exceeds 0.02 studs, any sleeping dynamic body on either side is woken so correction continues, and sleep returns naturally once the joint is tight; (2) the NGS pass now runs adaptive iterations (up to 10 while unconverged, early-out when satisfied), so sudden loads on high mass-ratio chains recover in a couple of frames instead of lingering. The exact runtime scenario (aggressive sleep, density masses, 8 links plus heavy tip under Roblox gravity) is now pinned as a headless contract test requiring the chain to settle tight AND still fall asleep. The runtime QA script was also fixed: Parts in this engine expose Rotation (XYZ euler order), not Orientation, which had silently killed the motor, servo and limit scene checks; the motor scene now validates spin speed and direction through AssemblyAngularVelocity.

entries.title: Physics: Hinge Motor Direction Fixed (Servo Converges, Limits Contain)
entries.description: Deep review of the positional stabilization work caught a serious hidden sign bug in the hinge motor: the engine drove the relative angular velocity with the opposite sign of the hinge angle measured by the game layer (and by Roblox). A positive AngularVelocity spun the wheel in the negative axis direction, Servo mode diverged away from TargetAngle instead of converging (positive feedback), and LimitsEnabled pushed the arm further OUT of its limits instead of back inside. The engine motor now follows the Roblox convention: motorSpeed is the rate of the hinge angle of Attachment1's body relative to Attachment0's body around the axis. The contract is pinned by new headless tests: the motor test now asserts the positive spin direction, and a new test reproduces the exact Servo feedback loop used by the game layer and asserts convergence to 45 degrees. A runtime QA script (tools/qa/parte108-teste-runtime.luau) builds five self-checking scenes automatically: a heavy chain, a motorized wheel, a servo arm, a motor pushing against limits and a box stack.

entries.title: Physics: Real Positional Stabilization (Split Impulse + NGS)
entries.description: First of three parts attacking the joint-stretching limitation. The solver no longer relies on simplified Baumgarte bias, which injected corrective energy into real velocities and let long chains or aggressive motors visibly stretch joints under load. Contacts now use split impulse: penetration is resolved through separate pseudo-velocities that move bodies out of overlap without adding kinetic energy, so depenetration never catapults bodies, restitution still works and resting stacks still fall asleep. Native joints (PointToPoint and Hinge) gain a Non-linear Gauss-Seidel position pass after integration that corrects pivot separation and hinge axis misalignment directly on positions and orientations, with slop tolerances and per-step correction caps so corrections stay stable; the pass runs a configurable number of iterations (solver.positionIterations, default 3, anti-exploit clamped to 0..10). Result: a 12-link chain with a 20x heavier tip under Roblox gravity keeps every link gap under 0.05 studs, and a motor at speed 20 with unlimited force no longer displaces its pivot. A new headless suite (jointStab108) covers chains, heavy pendulums, depenetration energy, restitution, stacking, motors, sleep regressions and fuzz inputs. Parts 2/3 and 3/3 will move Rope/Prismatic into native solver constraints and give BallSocket a hard cone limit.

entries.title: Sun Rays: Small Uncovered Slivers Now Emit Rays
entries.description: Fixed the remaining occlusion artifact where a small uncovered sliver of the sun (for example when a wall hides 95% of it) produced no rays or glow at all, as if fully covered. The root cause was the ray source being a purely analytic sun disc whose brightness fades to almost zero across the outer 60% of its radius: when geometry covered the bright center, the visible sliver of the real rendered sun fell in that near-zero fade zone and contributed nothing. The source is now driven by the actual rendered brightness of the sky: the luminance of the frame, gated by the sky occlusion mask (so bright parts or neon in front of the sun never emit) and by a radial window around the true sun position (so bright horizon or clouds elsewhere never emit). The analytic core remains only as a guaranteed floor. Any visible fraction of the sun, however small and wherever the wall cuts it, now emits rays and halo proportional to what is actually on screen, fading smoothly from fully open to fully covered.

entries.title: Sun Rays: Dense Sampling and Visible Defaults
entries.description: Deep review of the new sun rays caught three real problems reported in testing. The radial blur used only 16 samples along the path to the sun, so far from the sun the gap between samples became larger than the sun disc itself: rays vanished entirely when a wall covered around 60% of the sun (as if fully covered), and because the disc is aspect-corrected (narrower horizontally on widescreen), horizontal rays died much earlier than vertical ones, creating the asymmetric occlusion where covering the side half also killed the uncovered side. Sampling is now 48 taps per pass (over 2300 virtual taps with the two chained passes), so partial cover produces proportional, symmetric rays in every direction. The occlusion mask also renders at half resolution for crisper edges. Finally, the default effect was nearly invisible: energy was normalized too conservatively. The composite now applies a 3x stronger energy scale plus a soft halo of the visible sun disc, so a freshly inserted SunRaysEffect with default Intensity 0.25 is clearly visible like in Roblox.

entries.title: Sun Rays Faithful to Roblox (Real Sun Occlusion)
entries.description: SunRaysEffect no longer uses the old luminance-based radial shader that treated any bright pixel as a light source. The new pass reproduces the Roblox behavior: rays are born on the disc of the real sun (the same sun the sky and lighting use, following ClockTime and GeographicLatitude) and are physically blocked by scene geometry. A quarter-resolution occlusion mask marks where the sky is visible, the sun disc is drawn only where it is not covered, and a two-stage radial blur toward the sun stretches the visible light into rays with normalized decaying weights so energy stays stable. Spread controls the reach and softness of the rays as well as the apparent disc size, and Intensity controls the additive strength, fading automatically at dusk and when the sun leaves the screen or goes behind the camera. This closes the post-processing rewrite started in Part 105: all five Lighting effects (Bloom, Blur, ColorCorrection, DepthOfField, SunRays) are now custom implementations faithful to Roblox, and the corresponding limitation note was removed from the README.

entries.title: Depth of Field: Roblox Default Focus and Softer Near Bleeding
entries.description: Two fixes based on real usage. First, the default FocusDistance was 50, so with a freshly inserted DepthOfFieldEffect the sharp band sat at 40-60 studs and everything near the camera (including parts 7-10 studs away and the ground) was heavily blurred. Roblox's real default is 0.05, which keeps everything within about 10 studs of the camera perfectly sharp and blurs only the distance - the default now matches Roblox in the class definition, the sanitizer and the shader path. Second, the foreground bleeding used the spread blur alpha from both the half and quarter resolution levels at full strength, so close geometry at the bottom of the screen (like the ground) leaked blur over parts that should be in focus. The bleed now uses only the half resolution spread, keeping it local and subtle.

entries.title: Depth of Field Review: Sky Depth Corruption Fixed
entries.description: Deep review of the new Depth of Field pass caught three hidden issues before they reached users. Most importantly, the skybox is drawn by the renderer background system, which ignores the depth override material - so the sky COLORS were being written into the depth buffer and decoded as random distances, making sky pixels flicker between sharp and blurred. The depth render now temporarily removes the background (empty sky = maximum distance, which is correct) and restores it afterwards. The scene state (override material, background, clear color, shadow auto-update) is restored in a finally block so a mid-render error can never leak a corrupted state into the editor. Shadow maps are also frozen during the extra depth render, avoiding a double shadow pass per frame. Finally, all blur targets (DoF and BlurEffect) now derive their size from the real device-pixel buffer instead of the logical window size, so blur strength is consistent on hiDPI screens and no longer changes after the first window resize.

entries.title: Depth of Field Faithful to Roblox (Real Scene Depth)
entries.description: DepthOfFieldEffect no longer uses three.js BokehPass. The new custom pass reads the real depth of the scene and reproduces Roblox semantics exactly: everything inside FocusDistance +/- InFocusRadius stays perfectly sharp; blur ramps up smoothly outside the band, with NearIntensity controlling the near side (saturating at the camera) and FarIntensity the far side (thin-lens falloff saturating at the horizon). Blur runs progressively at 1/2 and 1/4 resolution with real gaussian kernels, and the near-field circle of confusion is blurred alongside the color so out-of-focus foreground objects bleed softly over the sharp background (as in Roblox) instead of having razor-sharp silhouettes. The circle-of-confusion math lives in the pure testable core with parameter sanitization (anti-exploit clamps), and the effect turns itself into a zero-cost passthrough when both intensities are 0.

entries.title: Hover/Select No Longer Loses Material State (Root Cause Cut)
entries.description: Hovering or selecting a Neon part made it lose its glow - and this was the third occurrence of the same hidden pattern in the project (a promoted part previously lost its material texture, then its visibility flag). Root cause: whenever a part is promoted out of an instanced pool or the lighting Technology changes, its material is recreated and the old code copied properties through hand-maintained whitelists scattered across call sites, silently dropping anything new (this time, the Neon emissive - which could not even survive because MeshBasicMaterial has no emissive channel to copy from). The pattern is now cut at the root: Neon's glow desire is stored declaratively in the material's userData (it exists on every material type), and a single canonical transferMaterialState helper enumerates ALL managed visual state (color, texture, transparency, opacity, side, vertex colors, visibility, declarative emissive) and is used by every material-replacement site, while shader patch flags (GI/PCSS) deliberately never migrate so rebuilt materials start clean. Future material states get added in one place and automatically survive hover, selection, Technology switches and the shader safe mode. New regression tests cover the declarative state, the transfer helper and the absence of leftover whitelists.

entries.title: Neon Parts Glow Again (Self-Lit Like Roblox)
entries.description: Deep-review fix for the faithful Bloom: Neon parts stopped glowing because their brightness was still multiplied by scene light, so with the real Roblox Threshold semantics (default 1.0) a neon pixel almost never crossed the soft knee - the old UnrealBloomPass only caught it because its threshold was remapped to roughly half. Neon is now truly self-lit like in Roblox: instanced pools inject an emissive term derived from each instance's own diffuse color directly in the shader (surviving the shader safe mode and keeping per-instance colors), and individual parts mirror the exact same energy through the material emissive channel, so a part never flickers when selection promotes it out of a pool. Neon now glows in shade and at night even without any BloomEffect, crosses Threshold 1 with a strong margin, resets cleanly when a part's material changes away from Neon, and the review also hardened the BlurEffect parameter guard against invalid property values. New regression tests cover the emissive shader patch, the pool/individual energy parity and the threshold-crossing math.

entries.title: Roblox-Faithful Post Effects (1/3): Bloom & Blur
entries.description: BloomEffect and BlurEffect no longer piggyback on generic three.js addon passes. Bloom is now a custom HDR mip chain: a soft-knee luminance prefilter driven directly by Threshold, progressive box downsampling with a gaussian pass per level, and a weighted six-level composite whose weights center on the pyramid level matching Size in pixels, so Intensity, Size and Threshold behave like the real Roblox properties instead of being remapped onto UnrealBloomPass knobs. BlurEffect is now a true separable gaussian whose sigma derives from Size in pixels, with linear-sampling tap pairs computed on the CPU and automatic half, quarter or eighth resolution execution for large radii, replacing the old fixed 9-tap approximation. All parameter math lives in a pure headless-testable core (src/viewport/postfxCore.js) with anti-exploit clamps on every input, render targets are reallocated only on resize or plan changes, and a new suite (postfx105) covers the mapping. Parts 2/3 and 3/3 will rebuild DepthOfFieldEffect and SunRaysEffect the same way.

entries.title: Skin-Weighted Mesh Decimation for Rigged Characters
entries.description: Skinned meshes now get real geometric LOD. The grid-clustering decimator carries skinIndex/skinWeight through clustering by accumulating per-bone weights inside each cluster, keeping the four strongest influences and renormalizing them to sum exactly 1, so deformation stays mathematically correct on every level. Each rigged mesh builds full/near/far levels (built once per geometry and cached), the solid and wireframe views swap together by camera distance with 5% hysteresis so the threshold never flickers, and re-importing or rebinding a mesh always restores the full geometry first. Meshes with morph targets or under the 300-triangle floor keep full detail, instancing pools still refuse skinned geometry (GPU instancing cannot animate skeletons), and combined with the animation-cadence LOD from the previous update this closes the skinned-mesh LOD limitation without needing impostors. Covered by a new headless test suite.

entries.title: Smooth Animation LOD for Skinned Meshes
entries.description: Distant skinned meshes no longer snap back to their rest pose. The old binary cutoff froze every rigged character past 250 studs and popped it back to life when the camera crossed the threshold; animation now keeps playing at every distance, with the pose update cadence scaling down instead — full rate up close, about 7.5 poses per second between 250 and 600 studs, and 2.5 per second beyond that — which keeps the old CPU savings without the visual pop. Bringing a character back into view refreshes its pose immediately and approaching one re-poses it within the tighter cadence of the new distance band, so a stale pose is never shown; idle rigs cost zero pose work once their last pose is applied, and the final frame of an animation always lands even at the lowest cadence. Covered by a new headless test suite.

entries.title: Distance LOD for Medium-Density Meshes
entries.description: The decimation floors dropped from 1200 (CSG unions) / 1500 (MeshParts, .obj and glTF pools) to 300 triangles, so medium meshes finally earn distance LOD levels instead of always rendering at full detail. The grid-clustering decimator now adapts its cell resolution to the source triangle count — coarser grids for lighter meshes, capped at the previous 44/16 so dense assets keep exactly the levels they had before — and retries once with a 30% coarser grid when the first pass fails the 25% minimum-gain gate, which also rescues the 1500–2500 triangle band that previously passed the floor but silently failed to compress. Swap distances, the 10% hysteresis and the 25% quality gate are unchanged, and the 600k-vertex build guard stays as an anti-freeze cap; covered by a new headless test suite.

entries.title: Distance LOD for glTF Instancing Pools
entries.description: Pooled glTF/GLB MeshParts no longer render at full triangle count at any distance. Instancing pools built from glTF assets (Part 84) now get the same distance-based LOD as CSG and .obj pools: each submesh of the shared prototype is decimated into aligned near/far levels (built once per asset and cached, reusing the per-geometry mesh LOD cache), and the whole pool swaps levels atomically — the primary InstancedMesh and every extra submesh InstancedMesh switch geometry together, chosen by the closest instance to the camera with the same 10% hysteresis as the individual path. Submeshes below the decimation floor simply keep their full geometry at every level so mixed assets still qualify, level distances are unified conservatively across submeshes (the largest per-submesh threshold wins and distances are forced strictly ascending), any LOD build failure gracefully falls back to the previous full-detail behavior, and the aligned-levels contract is covered by a new headless test suite.

entries.title: Real Mesh Colliders (Hull & Decomposition)
entries.description: CollisionFidelity now does what it says for imported meshes and CSG unions. On mesh import (.obj and non-skinned glTF/GLB), the editor builds real collision data in the mesh's normalized space: a true 3D convex hull (incremental quickhull with a deterministic vertex cap) and a box decomposition via voxelization (triangle-box SAT rasterization plus an outside flood-fill, so arches, tunnels and holes stay open instead of colliding in mid-air, even for non-watertight meshes). Hull uses the convex hull, Default and PreciseConvexDecomposition use the decomposition (falling back to the hull, then to the old fitted box), and union Hull now uses a real quickhull of the CSG mesh instead of its AABB. Colliders scale per-axis with Part.Size exactly like the visual, work for static and dynamic bodies through the existing compound-shape path, and every stage is capped and guarded so degenerate or oversized meshes safely fall back to the previous behavior. Deep review: script raycasts (workspace:Raycast) against MeshParts now hit the same real collider as the physics (box decomposition or hull, with the fitted box as fallback) instead of the full bounding box, quickhull conflict lists became single-owner so a point already absorbed by the hull can never be re-expanded through a stale face, every hull passes a containment self-check before being accepted, and per-axis extreme vertices always join the hull sample so heavily decimated meshes cannot get an undersized collider.

entries.title: glTF MeshPart Instancing
entries.description: Imported glTF/GLB props no longer pay one full mesh hierarchy per copy. Identical non-skinned MeshParts that reuse the same glTF asset now render as GPU instances: each submesh of the asset becomes a single InstancedMesh sharing one instance-matrix buffer with the group (up to 12 submeshes per asset), node transforms are baked into shared geometry built once per asset, and the asset's own materials are cloned once per pool instead of once per copy, keeping textures shared by reference. TextureID overrides and DoubleSided follow the exact semantics of the individual path, selection, hover, box-select, streaming visibility and the flat view modes keep working through instance promotion, and skinned or multi-material glTF scenes stay on the individual path so animation and per-group materials are never broken.

entries.title: Translucent Union Instancing
entries.description: Glass-like CSG unions (Transparency between 0 and 1) now join the complex-geometry instancing pools instead of paying one mesh, one draw call and one full boolean bake per copy. Pools are keyed by the effective transparency bucket and the pool material mirrors the individual path exactly: opacity = (1 - t) x base material opacity, staying in sync when material variants or the 2022/classic material toggle change it live. Each translucent pool anchors itself at its first instance so Three.js sorts it correctly against other transparent objects, and the instances inside a pool are re-sorted back to front whenever the camera moves or the pool changes, so glass seen through glass keeps blending correctly within a single draw call. Fully invisible parts stay on the individual path so their Decals remain visible, and edits that cross the opaque/translucent boundary migrate between pools automatically.

entries.title: Complex Geometry Instancing
entries.description: Scenes packed with duplicated complex geometry no longer pay one mesh and one draw call per copy. Identical CSG unions now share a single baked boolean geometry (built once and cached) and render as GPU instances in one draw call per group, keeping per-instance colors, the Neon boost, base-material and variant textures, and the exact physics collider snapshot. MeshParts that reuse the same .obj asset (same MeshId, TextureID and DoubleSided) are batched the same way through the shared geometry cache. Each pool picks its LOD level by camera distance with hysteresis, and selection, hover, box-select, lighting, streaming visibility and the Albedo/Roughness view modes keep working: instances are promoted to individual meshes on demand and return to the pool afterwards without rebuilding the boolean. Anti-exploit caps bound the number of pools, cached CSG geometries and mesh prototypes, and failed boolean builds are marked and never retried in a loop.

entries.title: Real Stream-In Identity
entries.description: Streaming now matches real Roblox identity semantics on the official Luau VM: when an instance streams back into range, client scripts receive a brand-new Lua object. References captured before the stream-out become permanent husks (Parent reads nil, no children, searches come up empty, writes stay blocked) even after the instance returns, and oldRef == workspace.Part is false after a stream-out/in cycle — exactly the production behavior that previously only appeared on the real platform. New lookups (WaitForChild, FindFirstChild, ChildAdded) hand out the fresh identity and copies of the same old reference still compare equal to each other. Deep review: connections and Wait calls made before the stream-out now die on re-stream-in instead of resurrecting, stale references cross remotes as nil, and instances not streamed to a client arrive as nil in RemoteEvent/RemoteFunction payloads on that client, matching production. The legacy JS engine keeps the previous reuse behavior as a documented fallback.

entries.title: Real Instance Streaming
entries.description: Workspace streaming is no longer a simulated replication filter: with StreamingEnabled, each Client now truly unloads out-of-range instances, matching real Roblox behavior. Held references become husks (Parent reads nil, GetFullName collapses, ancestor lookups fail), events such as Touched and Changed stop arriving for streamed-out instances, client raycasts and spatial queries ignore them, WaitForChild correctly waits for stream-in, indexing a streamed-out child raises the standard member error, and writes to unloaded instances are blocked with a warning. Workspace.PersistentLoaded now fires per client once persistent models finish replicating, visible in the Streaming Debug panel and covered by a new headless test suite.

entries.title: Binary Roblox Files (.rbxl / .rbxm)
entries.description: The File menu now exports and imports the native binary Roblox formats. Export to Roblox (.rbxl) saves the whole place and Export Selection to Roblox (.rbxm) saves the selection as compact LZ4-compressed binaries that open directly in the official Roblox Studio, and Import now auto-detects binary files by signature regardless of extension. The binary codec is a pure transcoder that reuses the battle-tested .rbxlx pipeline, with strict anti-exploit limits (50MB files, 100k instances, decompression caps) and graceful warnings for unknown chunks and property types.

entries.title: Debugger: Step Into Coroutines & Writable Locals
entries.description: Step Into now follows execution into user-created coroutines (coroutine.create, coroutine.wrap, task.spawn), and Step Over/Out correctly returns to the resumer when a coroutine finishes. The Watch panel can now assign to locals and upvalues of the paused frame (e.g. hp = 50 changes the real value, reflected immediately in Locals). Requires the Part 77 wasm rebuild; older binaries keep working with graceful degradation.

entries.title: Massive Scene Performance
entries.description: The editor now scales to tens of thousands of parts. Simple Plastic/SmoothPlastic parts are batched into GPU-instanced meshes (a handful of draw calls instead of one per part), with instances promoted to individual meshes on the fly for selection, hover, lights and adornments. The Explorer tree is virtualized and only renders the visible rows, keeping search, rename, drag & drop and Server/Client views intact. Saves and exports reuse an incremental per-instance serialization cache that is invalidated by property, attribute and lifetime events. The viewport render cap was raised from 1,500 to 50,000 objects.

entries.title: Exact CSG Engine
entries.description: Solid Modeling was rebuilt on an exact mesh-boolean engine: BVH-accelerated triangle intersection, convex fragmentation, ray-parity and winding-number classification, and explicit coplanar face handling replace the old BSP approximation. Unions, negations and intersections now produce watertight, artifact-free results even for touching, identical, rotated or degenerate geometry, with sanitized inputs and a 150,000-triangle anti-exploit cap per boolean operation.

entries.title: Full Luau — Official VM (WebAssembly)
entries.description: Scripts now run on the official Luau VM compiled to WebAssembly: 100% of the language (full metatables, native coroutines, string interpolation, continue, buffer, vector, string.pack, real incremental GC) with official bytecode performance. The legacy JS interpreter remains as automatic fallback and for Debugger breakpoints (Studio Settings > Script Editor > Luau Engine).

entries.title: Roblox Studio Interop (.rbxlx / .rbxmx)
entries.description: Export your place as a real .rbxlx file and your selection as .rbxmx, both openable in the official Roblox Studio. Import .rbxlx/.rbxmx files back with full undo support: parts keep CFrame rotation, colors, materials, surfaces, scripts (including exotic sources) and object references.

entries.title: Version 1.0.0 — Project Complete
entries.description: All 68 development parts are finished. Roblox Studio Web is now feature-complete and stable for real use as a development and learning tool.

entries.title: Master Validation
entries.description: Run 33 automated integrity checks from Test > Validation (Ctrl+Alt+V): core state, EventBus health, serialization round-trips, full Play/Run cycles with snapshot verification, CSG, pathfinding, localization, DataStores, badges, multi-client, streaming and performance benchmarks. Export the full report as JSON.

entries.title: Final Integration Fixes
entries.description: Fixed Terrain duplicating after every Run/Stop cycle (snapshot restore). Monaco Editor shortcuts like Ctrl+D are no longer stolen by global actions while typing. Highlight and SelectionBox now track UnionOperations correctly without z-fighting. DragDetectors respect streaming; the Developer Console Memory tab reflects the streamed client; the MicroProfiler no longer stalls with multiple clients.

entries.title: Help System & API Browser
entries.description: A complete Help menu with About dialog, Welcome Tour and bug reporting. The new dockable API Browser lets you explore every class, enum and library without leaving the editor.

entries.title: Editor Notifications
entries.description: A new Notification Center collects editor events in one place. Toasts appear in the bottom-right corner with auto-dismiss and quick actions.

entries.title: Studio AI Assistant & Code Assist
entries.description: Chat with an AI assistant directly inside Studio to generate scripts and answer questions. Inline Code Assist suggests Luau completions as you type.

entries.title: Assistant Panel Stability Fixes
entries.description: Fixed rendering glitches in the assistant panel when switching conversations. Provider errors no longer leave the send button stuck.

entries.title: Package Manager
entries.description: Create, publish and update packages from reusable models. Version bumps propagate to every place that uses the package.

entries.title: Team Create & Version History
entries.description: Collaborate with simulated teammates in real time, follow their cameras and review drafts. Version History lets you restore any previous save.

entries.title: Drafts & Activity Log
entries.description: Script drafts keep your edits separate until you commit them. The Activity Log shows who changed what and when.

entries.title: Plugin Menus & Toolbars
entries.description: Plugins can now register custom menus and toolbar buttons. Manage everything from the Plugins tab in the menu bar.

entries.title: Material Manager Improvements
entries.description: Preview materials on a sphere before applying them. Custom material variants are grouped per base material.

entries.title: Localization Tools
entries.description: Translate your game with the localization table editor, CSV import and export, and automatic pseudo-translation during Playtest.

entries.title: Sound System Upgrades
entries.description: Sound instances support playback speed, looping and rolloff settings. SoundService groups make mixing easier.

entries.title: Lighting & Atmosphere
entries.description: Atmosphere, Sky and post-processing effects render more accurately. Time of day updates the sun position in real time.

entries.title: Keybinding Editor & Studio Settings
entries.description: Remap any shortcut from the new Keybinding Editor. Studio Settings centralizes every editor preference in one dialog.

entries.title: Start Page
entries.description: Pick a template, reopen recent projects or browse My Games from the redesigned Start Page.

entries.title: Terrain Editor Improvements
entries.description: Sculpting brushes are smoother and support adjustable strength. Painting materials on terrain is faster on large maps.

entries.title: Playtest CoreGui
entries.description: The simulated player experience now includes chat, leaderboard, backpack and health bar during Playtest.

entries.title: Multi-Client Playtest
entries.description: Start a server with multiple simulated clients to test replication. Switch between client and server views while testing.

entries.title: GUI Editor Enhancements
entries.description: Drag-and-drop editing for ScreenGuis with snap guides and alignment tools. UI constraints preview live in the viewport.

entries.title: Tag Editor & CollectionService
entries.description: Organize instances with tags and query them from scripts using CollectionService.

entries.title: Luau Debugger
entries.description: Set breakpoints, step through code and inspect variables while your scripts run.

entries.title: Auto-Save & Recovery

entries.title: Toolbox
entries.description: Browse free models, images and audio in the Toolbox and insert them directly into your place.

entries.title: Script Analysis
entries.description: The analyzer flags undefined variables, type mismatches and deprecated APIs while you type.

entries.description: Full autocomplete for the Roblox API with hover documentation and signature help in the Script Editor.
